description: RabbitMQ (dt-broker) pod, node and queue status
title: RabbitMQ Health Monitoring

panels.title: Pods ready
panels.description: Ready RabbitMQ pods (kube-state-metrics). Should equal desired replicas.

panels.title: Nodes reporting
panels.description: RabbitMQ nodes Prometheus is scraping right now.

panels.title: Active alarms
panels.description: Memory, disk and file-descriptor alarms. Any alarm blocks publishers.

panels.title: Pod status
panels.description: One row per RabbitMQ pod: readiness, phase, restarts in the selected range, Prometheus scrape status, node and RabbitMQ alarms.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_memory_used_watermark{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}) + max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_free_disk_space_watermark{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"}) + max by (pod) (rabbitmq_alarms_file_descriptor_limit{namespace=~"$namespace",pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: CPU usage vs limit
panels.description: CPU cores used by the rabbitmq container.

panels.title: RabbitMQ memory vs high watermark
panels.description: Resident memory as a fraction of vm_memory_high_watermark. At 100% the memory alarm blocks publishers.

panels.title: Free disk vs alarm limit
panels.description: If free disk drops under disk_free_limit, the disk alarm blocks publishers.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: Restarts in a sliding 15m window. Alert fires above 3.

panels.title: Queue status by pod
panels.description: Queue numbers summed per RabbitMQ pod. Each queue is counted on the pod that hosts its leader.

panels.title: Messages ready / unacked (cluster)
panels.description: Ready = waiting to be picked up (backlog). Unacked = picked up but not yet confirmed by the consumer.

panels.title: Consumers and queues
panels.description: Consumers dropping to 0 while messages are ready means nothing is processing the backlog.

panels.title: Unroutable messages
panels.description: Messages published to an exchange with no matching binding. Usually a misconfigured routing key or a missing queue.

panels.title: Connection churn
panels.description: High churn means clients open a new connection per message instead of reusing one.
